svg.title: First one pocket. Then two.
svg.desc: The complete efficient total-area and smallest-pocket frontier for four cubic-intercept parabolas with outer labels one and three has two branches. First only triangle B grows. At labels about 1.825622 and 2.459833, triangles A and B tie; both then grow together until all three pockets are equal. A full frontier graph and an explicitly enlarged first-branch graph use different axis scales. Two complete arrangements below share coordinates and unit scale: the switch, and first interior label seven quarters. Their area table and slope rulers show the change. The exact global proof uses rational sign certificates; the graph samples, coordinates, and decimal readouts in this drawing are rounded illustrations.

g.text: Every point gives the largest total for its smallest-pocket requirement.
Four curves: Xₚ = Y²/2 − pY + p³/3. Outer slope labels: 1 and 3.
Largest total; switch just beside it.
Axis spans differ from the full graph.
Each percentage uses its own area at the largest-total placement as its baseline.
The second interior label first falls, then rises. Here are two stops along the way.
A and B grow together. C shrinks.
Both complete arrangements share coordinates and unit scale.
Keep the outer labels. Move both inner curves.
The proof covers every placement. The graph samples and printed decimals are rounded.

a.text: Follow both branches and the exact global certificate ↗
